title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), a single generator pairing (requested model: gpt-5-mini), and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). The run used shared-initial-candidate generation semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations materially affect inference and are explicitly reported: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, the results show that bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in the executed archive-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct; the outcome does not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, repair budget, or verifier.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) can improve NetOps productivity but introduces operational risk: stochastic generators may emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow safety, policy/ACL predicates). Prior work therefore recommends architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment asking a precise operational question: under a frozen, archived design that used a single generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative for the reported quantities.
sections.related_work: Three strands ground this study. (1) LLM failure modes and hallucination: surveys and empirical case studies document hallucinations and fabricated outputs for code and structured artifacts, motivating deterministic validators in downstream pipelines. (2) Generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding architectures: prior systems and case studies report improvements on mechanically checkable properties (e.g., compilability, grammar validity) when generation is combined with validation and repair, but domain-level semantic guarantees remain open. (3) NetOps-specific verification and intent translation: intent-based systems, topology-aware verifiers, and human-in-the-loop governance features are recurrently recommended to prevent unsafe changes. Our run differs in two ways: it is fully preregistered and archived, and it uses a paired confirmatory design with an explicit deterministic validator oracle to measure verifier-detectable differences attributable to a bounded GVR intervention.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: The experiment was preregistered (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the paired difference in the proportion of tasks with verifier-detected semantic violations (computed by a preregistered paired-binary analysis executor). Two prespecified primary comparisons were listed: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding with Bonferroni correction across the two. Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory sample N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). Requested generator: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial frozen execution semantics (as archived): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); maximum_model_calls budget = 480; execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. Plain-language executed-methods summary (per reviewer request and archived values): one shared initial generation per task was produced and reused by both arms (therefore model_calls_used = 240), a single bounded repair attempt was permitted per task but repairs were only invoked if the verifier reported a violation, and the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied explicit intent→state predicate checks (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count) for scoring.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 under the shared-initial-candidate semantics. Representative scoring artifacts show the shared initial candidate was identical to both arm responses for every task. Primary confirmatory outcomes: The preregistered analysis executor produced the contingency table n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Observed rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Repair usage: repair_applied = false for every episode because every shared initial candidate satisfied the verifier; therefore the bounded repair loop never executed. Missingness and contamination: analysis/missingness_summary.csv and analysis/contamination_summary.csv report zero failures and zero flags.
sections.discussion: Statistical degeneracy and its cause: The observed contingency (zero discordant pairs) makes the paired-test degenerate: no within-pair disagreements exist to estimate an effect. The exact McNemar p = 1.00 and the bootstrap CI collapsing to [0.0, 0.0] are deterministic consequences of the contingency under the preregistered analysis executor and the recorded bootstrap parameters. This degeneracy traces directly to the executed shared-generation semantics, which removed independent per-arm stochasticity and thereby eliminated the discordance that a repair intervention could exploit. Preregistration→execution deviations that affect inference: (1) Preregistered power calculations assumed independent per-condition generation; the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics violate that assumption and therefore invalidate the preregistered power argument for the observed run. (2) The preregistration prespecified two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B); the archive documents only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing the unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale for its omission appears in the execution artifacts. These two deviations are reported here explicitly and treated as unresolved procedural limitations. Practical implications for evaluation: To measure operational value of GVR under generator stochasticity, an evaluation must restore per-arm generation independence (independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks that induce verifier-detectable failures, broaden generator families, or expand the repair budget and verifier coverage. The archived artifacts already provide the task manifest and RNG seeds to rerun the preregistered independent-generation design deterministically.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered and archived paired evaluation of a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and the single generator pairing, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate and degenerate inferential outcomes (exact McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific archive-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. However, two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) the prespecified comparison vs a schema-constrained baseline was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archive. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts to enable deterministic reruns under independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model regimes to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
